answer: Conclusion: binding one identity kernel to one public key makes sybil attacks uneconomical. Like a raven returning to a single nest, each agent keeps one vertex of trust: its kernel, signed by its key, earns non-transferable reputation only through peer-graded work. A random jury of established, unrelated peers checks each claim, so fake identities cannot attest for each other. Creating N fake agents then costs N times the work, stake, and cipher-signed history, while an honest agent pays only once.
